report.summary: recommendationservice pods are being OOMKilled immediately after startup following the revision 6 deployment on 2026-08-03. Both revision 6 (37 restarts, exit_code=137) and revision 7 (3+ restarts, OOMKilled) pods exhibit identical memory exhaustion patterns. Kernel terminates container for exceeding memory limit; kubelet restarts it, creating a crash loop. Liveness and readiness probes timeout as process is killed before responding. Cluster nodes are healthy with no memory pressure, and image tag unchanged between revisions, confirming the pod's memory limit is insufficient for the workload.
report.root_cause: Container memory limit exceeded; kernel OOMKills the recommendationservice process, triggering an uncontrolled restart loop
evidence: Pod recommendationservice-649cdccf96-tr8sq status explicitly shows last_reason='OOMKilled', exit_code=137
Pod recommendationservice-58c6549c55-llfk6 from revision 6 shows 37 restarts with last_exit_code=137 (SIGKILL), same signature as revision 7

Event 2026-08-19T07:18:47Z: Liveness and readiness probes failed with 'timeout: failed to connect service 10.42.2.207:8080 within 1s: context deadline exceeded'—process unresponsive because kernel killed it for memory
Restart count climbing: revision 6 at 37 restarts since 2026-08-03T05:31:22Z, revision 7 at 3+ since 2026-08-19T07:18:44Z—classic OOMKill-and-restart loop signature
get_node_status reports MemoryPressure=False on k3d-sre-lab-agent-0 and k3d-sre-lab-agent-1—cluster has available memory, confirming pod limit is too low, not cluster exhaustion
Rollout history shows image tag v0.10.5 identical across revisions 1, 2, 3, 6, 7; ruling out binary code change as root cause
Same image v0.10.5 deployed successfully in revisions 1–3 (July 7–11) without reported restarts; memory exhaustion is new post-revision 6
alternatives: Revision 7 pod spec changed (resource limits, env vars, mounts modified) causing increased memory demand or reduced limit (0.65): Pod spec change confirmed in timeline but details unavailable; cannot verify if limit was reduced between revisions without manifest visibility; if limit reduced, expect immediate failure on next reconciliation, not 16-day degradation since rev 6

Application code v0.10.5 contains a memory leak accumulating until limit hit (0.4): Same image tag deployed successfully in revisions 1–3 (July 7–11) without reported restarts; if memory leak existed in v0.10.5, why was it not triggered in those earlier, stable deployments? No evidence of image retagging

Image tag v0.10.5 was retagged (pushed again) with different code containing memory leak (0.35): No image digest/hash change visible in tool outputs; would require external registry audit; speculation without verifiable evidence

Downstream dependency (database, cache, other microservice) is unavailable; recommendationservice retries/buffers, exhausting memory (0.25): Pod shows OOMKilled (direct memory limit violation), not secondary dependency failure; probe timeout is on pod's own port (10.42.2.207:8080), not downstream service; OOMKill is explicit and primary, not symptom of retry loop

Pod allocated insufficient CPU; cannot respond to liveness/readiness probes within 1s timeout; kubelet terminates after repeated failures (0.15): Exit code 137 is SIGKILL from memory, not CPU enforcement; OOMKilled is explicit in pod status, not a side-effect of probe failure termination; get_node_status shows no CPU pressure

Pod scheduled to node without sufficient available memory; crashes on startup (0.1): Pod phase is Running (scheduled successfully); if node was full, scheduler would not place pod; MemoryPressure=False on both nodes confirms available memory
report.impact: recommendationservice is unavailable in production due to persistent CrashLoopBackOff. Restart cycle began 2026-08-03 (revision 6) and continues through 2026-08-19 (revision 7). Pod has accumulated 37 restarts over 16+ days without achieving stable operation, indicating zero successful request processing during this entire period. Users cannot access recommendation functionality.

remediation.action: Increase memory limit for recommendationservice container
remediation.rationale: Pod is OOMKilled immediately after startup by kernel, indicating declared memory limit is lower than required for normal operation. Cluster nodes have available memory (MemoryPressure=False), and image is unchanged from earlier revisions, confirming the workload's memory demand exceeds its current allocation. Increasing limit to 1Gi provides headroom for stable operation. This is reversible and can be tuned further if needed.

correlation.summary: recommendationservice pods are OOMKilled immediately after startup following revision 7 deployment. Both revision 6 (37 restarts, exit 137) and revision 7 (3+ restarts, OOMKilled) pods show identical memory exhaustion pattern. No cluster-wide memory pressure. Image tag unchanged between revisions, indicating non-binary pod spec change triggered the issue. Liveness/readiness probes timeout as process is killed by kernel before responding. Nodes are healthy (MemoryPressure=False). Root cause is memory limit exceeded; fix requires investigating what pod spec changed in revision 7 and adjusting memory limits or removing the configuration that drives memory overconsumption.

Probe timeouts ('failed to connect service within 1s') are consistent with process being killed under memory pressure
Restart count climbing (37 on older pod, 3 on newer) matches behavior of OOMKill-and-restart cycle
against: No node-level MemoryPressure reported (get_node_status shows MemoryPressure=False on both nodes)
Same image tag v0.10.5 was deployed successfully in multiple earlier revisions (Rev 1–3 from July without issue)
